# Reinforcement learning

For new RL, RLVR or GRPO work with supported Olmo MoE models, use
`python -m open_instruct.miles` and follow [the MILES guide](docs/miles/grpo.md),
including its launch checks and configuration conventions. Existing Core/vLLM
(`grpo.py`) and DeepSpeed/vLLM (`grpo_fast.py`) workflows remain current alternatives
for dense-model training; see [their guide](docs/algorithms/grpo.md).
Choose according to model and workload support, preserve the user's selected
workflow, and identify support gaps explicitly. MILES does not deprecate the
existing GRPO trainers.

For MILES GPU runs on `ai2/jupiter` or `ai2/saturn` (CUDA 12.8 host drivers), keep
the pinned MILES image: RunSpec defaults `launch.env.LD_LIBRARY_PATH` to the image's
CUDA compatibility libraries, and an explicit value wins. Revalidate CUDA
initialization and a short training run when the image or driver changes. See
[Jupiter CUDA compatibility](docs/miles/launching.md#jupiter-cuda-compatibility).

# Bash commands
- `uv run pytest`: Run the tests.
- `make style && make quality` run the linter + formatter.
- `uv run mkdocs serve`: View the documentation locally at http://127.0.0.1:8000/
- `uv run mkdocs build`: Build the documentation to the `site/` directory.



## Code Review Rules

Read and follow [CODE_REVIEW.md](CODE_REVIEW.md) when reviewing code.

# Workflow
- Begin every GitHub comment published by an agent with one plain line naming the agent (e.g. Codex, Claude Code): `Drafted by {agent name}.`, with no alert or other formatting. If a person reviewed the response before publication, use `Drafted by {agent name} and reviewed by {reviewer's name}.` instead. Only include the review attribution when that person actually reviewed the response; permission to post alone does not count as review.
- When a PR changes anything under `open_instruct/`, add a summary to `CHANGELOG.md` with a link to the PR (e.g., `- Description of change (https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/pull/123).`). This is what CI enforces; PRs touching only `scripts/`, docs, or config are exempt, though an entry is still welcome for anything user-visible.
  - The entry must contain the PR's own URL, which does not exist until the PR is opened. Add the entry, open the PR, then amend the entry with the URL and push again.
  - To skip the check deliberately, put `CHANGELOG=<reason>` in the PR body.
- Always run the linter and make sure the tests pass before finishing a task.
- Prefer running single tests, not the whole suite, when developing.
- Launch Beaker experiment and test scripts with `./scripts/train/build_image_and_launch.sh [--cuda-version 12|13] SCRIPT` after committing all changes. CUDA 13 images are for compatible clusters such as `ai2/holmes`. MILES uses `--miles CONFIG` and its pinned runtime.
- For the Core/vLLM and DeepSpeed/vLLM GRPO workflows, we have three test scripts (for MILES checks, follow `docs/miles/architecture.md`):
  - `scripts/train/debug/single_gpu_on_beaker.sh`: single GPU, no tools (~8 minutes).
  - `scripts/train/debug/tools/olmo_3_parser_multigpu.sh`: multi GPU, with tools.
  - `scripts/train/debug/large_test_script.sh`: two 8x GPU nodes, no tools (~32 minutes).
- For OLMo-core SFT, we have two test scripts:
  - `scripts/train/debug/oc_sft.sh`: single GPU on Beaker.
  - `scripts/train/debug/oc_sft_multinode.sh`: two 8x GPU nodes on Beaker.
- For DPO, we have three test scripts:
  - `scripts/train/debug/dpo/local.sh`: local single GPU (no Beaker).
  - `scripts/train/debug/dpo/single_gpu.sh`: single GPU on Beaker.
  - `scripts/train/debug/dpo/multi_node.sh`: two 8x GPU nodes on Beaker.
- Launch the GPU tests with `./scripts/train/build_image_and_launch.sh scripts/test/run_gpu_pytest.sh`.
- CI runs on GitHub-hosted runners without Beaker experiments or image publication. Run GPU tests manually when a change touches GPU code paths. Record `GPU_TESTS=[EXPERIMENT_ID](https://beaker.org/ex/EXPERIMENT_ID)` in the PR body for reviewers; CI does not parse or verify this line, and `GPU_TESTS=bypass` has no effect. The experiment must actually run `scripts/test/run_gpu_pytest.sh`; record training/debug smoke runs separately. Existing `open_instruct_auto*` images are no longer refreshed by CI; build from the intended revision with the launcher.
- If you are given a Beaker URL (`beaker.org` or `beaker.allen.ai`), use the Beaker CLI tool to interact with it.
- When a Beaker job stays queued or pending, run `beaker job events <job-id>` before diagnosing why — it prints the scheduler's own reason; don't infer one from cluster documentation. If that reason is the workspace slot limit, it applies to every cluster at once: wait or request fewer GPUs rather than relaunching elsewhere.
- A Beaker experiment can hold several jobs when a preempted one is retried. Read the most recently created attempt for each task and replica rank, not `jobs[0]` or one latest job for the entire experiment, or a successful retry looks like a failure and missing replicas can be overlooked.
- Mason's `--min_runtime <duration>` sets Beaker's `minRuntime` (0, or a duration with a unit of at least 5m, such as `30m`; Ai2 clusters currently allow at most 8h), and `--auto_resume` sets `autoResume`. On allocation-scheduled clusters, a job with a min runtime above 0 is allocated: it queues ahead of backfill and is protected until its min runtime ends, and shorter min runtimes schedule sooner. Its workspace needs an allocation on that cluster, or Beaker rejects it at submission. The legacy `--preemptible` switch, which cannot be combined with `--min_runtime`, maps to `minRuntime: 0` and `autoResume: true`; such unallocated jobs run only as backfill and may wait indefinitely. Passing neither flag maps to an eight-hour protected, non-resumable job, the hardest kind to schedule. Prefer a realistic `--min_runtime` (the time the job needs to reach a checkpoint), and call out this choice before launching instead of silently copying a checked-in script's choice.
- On macOS, GRPO launch scripts that call `mason.py` need `--no_auto_dataset_cache` (before the `--` separator). Local dataset caching runs the training entrypoint with `--cache_dataset_only`, and `grpo.py` / `grpo_fast.py` still import vllm at module level (`grpo_fast.py` from `vllm.distributed.weight_transfer`, `grpo.py` via `vllm_utils`), which is not installed on Darwin. `finetune.py`, `dpo.py`, `dpo_tune_cache.py` and `reward_modeling.py` no longer import vllm on this path since [#1866](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/pull/1866), so their scripts do not need the flag. `mason.py` prints a macOS hint but still attempts caching, so it does not protect you either way.
- The `oe-eval-internal` directory is required in the Docker image for experiments that use `--try_launch_beaker_eval_jobs_on_weka`. If it's missing (e.g. in a fresh clone or worktree), clone it with: `git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/allenai/oe-eval-internal.git oe-eval-internal`.
- When updating PR bodies with experiment results, use the "Runs:" format (numbered list with Beaker links):
  ```
  Runs:

  1. Description: [Beaker](https://beaker.org/ex/EXPERIMENT_ID)
  2. Description: [Beaker](https://beaker.org/ex/EXPERIMENT_ID)
  ```

# Naming conventions
- Models OLMo and OLMo 2 (versions <=2) use the "OLMo" capitalization style.
- Olmo 3, Olmo Hybrid, and later models use "Olmo" (standard proper noun capitalization).
- Note: "OLMo-core" refers to the software repository and keeps its original capitalization.

# Coding conventions
- Never use `import logging` or `logging.info()` directly. Always use `logger = logger_utils.setup_logger(__name__)` and `logger.info()`.
- Imports always go at the top of the file, never inline.
- Use `from package import module` instead of `import package.module`.

# Documentation

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.

tools.name: ReportFindings

Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

# Reinforcement learning

For new RL, RLVR or GRPO work with supported Olmo MoE models, use
`python -m open_instruct.miles` and follow [the MILES guide](docs/miles/grpo.md),
including its launch checks and configuration conventions. Existing Core/vLLM
(`grpo.py`) and DeepSpeed/vLLM (`grpo_fast.py`) workflows remain current alternatives
for dense-model training; see [their guide](docs/algorithms/grpo.md).
Choose according to model and workload support, preserve the user's selected
workflow, and identify support gaps explicitly. MILES does not deprecate the
existing GRPO trainers.

For MILES GPU runs on `ai2/jupiter` or `ai2/saturn` (CUDA 12.8 host drivers), keep
the pinned MILES image: RunSpec defaults `launch.env.LD_LIBRARY_PATH` to the image's
CUDA compatibility libraries, and an explicit value wins. Revalidate CUDA
initialization and a short training run when the image or driver changes. See
[Jupiter CUDA compatibility](docs/miles/launching.md#jupiter-cuda-compatibility).

# Bash commands
- `uv run pytest`: Run the tests.
- `make style && make quality` run the linter + formatter.
- `uv run mkdocs serve`: View the documentation locally at http://127.0.0.1:8000/
- `uv run mkdocs build`: Build the documentation to the `site/` directory.



## Code Review Rules

Read and follow [CODE_REVIEW.md](CODE_REVIEW.md) when reviewing code.

# Workflow
- Begin every GitHub comment published by an agent with one plain line naming the agent (e.g. Codex, Claude Code): `Drafted by {agent name}.`, with no alert or other formatting. If a person reviewed the response before publication, use `Drafted by {agent name} and reviewed by {reviewer's name}.` instead. Only include the review attribution when that person actually reviewed the response; permission to post alone does not count as review.
- When a PR changes anything under `open_instruct/`, add a summary to `CHANGELOG.md` with a link to the PR (e.g., `- Description of change (https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/pull/123).`). This is what CI enforces; PRs touching only `scripts/`, docs, or config are exempt, though an entry is still welcome for anything user-visible.
  - The entry must contain the PR's own URL, which does not exist until the PR is opened. Add the entry, open the PR, then amend the entry with the URL and push again.
  - To skip the check deliberately, put `CHANGELOG=<reason>` in the PR body.
- Always run the linter and make sure the tests pass before finishing a task.
- Prefer running single tests, not the whole suite, when developing.
- Launch Beaker experiment and test scripts with `./scripts/train/build_image_and_launch.sh [--cuda-version 12|13] SCRIPT` after committing all changes. CUDA 13 images are for compatible clusters such as `ai2/holmes`. MILES uses `--miles CONFIG` and its pinned runtime.
- For the Core/vLLM and DeepSpeed/vLLM GRPO workflows, we have three test scripts (for MILES checks, follow `docs/miles/architecture.md`):
  - `scripts/train/debug/single_gpu_on_beaker.sh`: single GPU, no tools (~8 minutes).
  - `scripts/train/debug/tools/olmo_3_parser_multigpu.sh`: multi GPU, with tools.
  - `scripts/train/debug/large_test_script.sh`: two 8x GPU nodes, no tools (~32 minutes).
- For OLMo-core SFT, we have two test scripts:
  - `scripts/train/debug/oc_sft.sh`: single GPU on Beaker.
  - `scripts/train/debug/oc_sft_multinode.sh`: two 8x GPU nodes on Beaker.
- For DPO, we have three test scripts:
  - `scripts/train/debug/dpo/local.sh`: local single GPU (no Beaker).
  - `scripts/train/debug/dpo/single_gpu.sh`: single GPU on Beaker.
  - `scripts/train/debug/dpo/multi_node.sh`: two 8x GPU nodes on Beaker.
- Launch the GPU tests with `./scripts/train/build_image_and_launch.sh scripts/test/run_gpu_pytest.sh`.
- CI runs on GitHub-hosted runners without Beaker experiments or image publication. Run GPU tests manually when a change touches GPU code paths. Record `GPU_TESTS=[EXPERIMENT_ID](https://beaker.org/ex/EXPERIMENT_ID)` in the PR body for reviewers; CI does not parse or verify this line, and `GPU_TESTS=bypass` has no effect. The experiment must actually run `scripts/test/run_gpu_pytest.sh`; record training/debug smoke runs separately. Existing `open_instruct_auto*` images are no longer refreshed by CI; build from the intended revision with the launcher.
- If you are given a Beaker URL (`beaker.org` or `beaker.allen.ai`), use the Beaker CLI tool to interact with it.
- When a Beaker job stays queued or pending, run `beaker job events <job-id>` before diagnosing why — it prints the scheduler's own reason; don't infer one from cluster documentation. If that reason is the workspace slot limit, it applies to every cluster at once: wait or request fewer GPUs rather than relaunching elsewhere.
- A Beaker experiment can hold several jobs when a preempted one is retried. Read the most recently created attempt for each task and replica rank, not `jobs[0]` or one latest job for the entire experiment, or a successful retry looks like a failure and missing replicas can be overlooked.
- Mason's `--min_runtime <duration>` sets Beaker's `minRuntime` (0, or a duration with a unit of at least 5m, such as `30m`; Ai2 clusters currently allow at most 8h), and `--auto_resume` sets `autoResume`. On allocation-scheduled clusters, a job with a min runtime above 0 is allocated: it queues ahead of backfill and is protected until its min runtime ends, and shorter min runtimes schedule sooner. Its workspace needs an allocation on that cluster, or Beaker rejects it at submission. The legacy `--preemptible` switch, which cannot be combined with `--min_runtime`, maps to `minRuntime: 0` and `autoResume: true`; such unallocated jobs run only as backfill and may wait indefinitely. Passing neither flag maps to an eight-hour protected, non-resumable job, the hardest kind to schedule. Prefer a realistic `--min_runtime` (the time the job needs to reach a checkpoint), and call out this choice before launching instead of silently copying a checked-in script's choice.
- On macOS, GRPO launch scripts that call `mason.py` need `--no_auto_dataset_cache` (before the `--` separator). Local dataset caching runs the training entrypoint with `--cache_dataset_only`, and `grpo.py` / `grpo_fast.py` still import vllm at module level (`grpo_fast.py` from `vllm.distributed.weight_transfer`, `grpo.py` via `vllm_utils`), which is not installed on Darwin. `finetune.py`, `dpo.py`, `dpo_tune_cache.py` and `reward_modeling.py` no longer import vllm on this path since [#1866](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/pull/1866), so their scripts do not need the flag. `mason.py` prints a macOS hint but still attempts caching, so it does not protect you either way.
- The `oe-eval-internal` directory is required in the Docker image for experiments that use `--try_launch_beaker_eval_jobs_on_weka`. If it's missing (e.g. in a fresh clone or worktree), clone it with: `git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/allenai/oe-eval-internal.git oe-eval-internal`.
- When updating PR bodies with experiment results, use the "Runs:" format (numbered list with Beaker links):
  ```
  Runs:

  1. Description: [Beaker](https://beaker.org/ex/EXPERIMENT_ID)
  2. Description: [Beaker](https://beaker.org/ex/EXPERIMENT_ID)
  ```

# Naming conventions
- Models OLMo and OLMo 2 (versions <=2) use the "OLMo" capitalization style.
- Olmo 3, Olmo Hybrid, and later models use "Olmo" (standard proper noun capitalization).
- Note: "OLMo-core" refers to the software repository and keeps its original capitalization.

# Coding conventions
- Never use `import logging` or `logging.info()` directly. Always use `logger = logger_utils.setup_logger(__name__)` and `logger.info()`.
- Imports always go at the top of the file, never inline.
- Use `from package import module` instead of `import package.module`.

# Documentation
To verify that documentation changes don't alter the generated output:

129	
130	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
131	
132	`compile()` 是两层配置之间的翻译器：把结构化 run 文件里「研究者语言」的节（`[training]`、`[trainer]`、`[inference]`……）翻译成底层引擎消费的 `core.*` 与 `miles.*` 选项，套上工作流默认值，做跨字段的容量算术（GPU 整除、上下文长度、批大小），最后组装成 `RunConfig(CoreConfig(...), miles_options)` 并整体校验。`CoreConfig` 是 Core 训练引擎的开关集合（frozen dataclass），`RunConfig` 把它与 miles 选项字典合在一起做联合合法性检查，并能编译出真正的命令行参数列表。
133	
134	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
135	
136	```text
137	RunSpec.compile(prepared=None)
138	  ├─ put(target, value, origin)：一切设置的唯一入口
139	  │    ├─ miles 键经 options.resolve_option 归一化（别名→规范名）
140	  │    ├─ 路径键解析为绝对路径
141	  │    ├─ 逐值即时校验（miles 走选项快照 + runtime_values；core 试构造 CoreConfig）
142	  │    └─ origins 记录来源；同目标不同值 → 冲突报错
143	  ├─ RUN_SECTIONS 各键分发：SPECIAL_CONTROLS / FIELD_MAP / core.* / miles.*
144	  ├─ [core] 与 [miles] 显式选项、compiler_cache、records、selection 依次 put
145	  ├─ 拓扑算术：world、rollout GPU 数、TP 整除、colocate 一致性、上下文/响应长度
146	  ├─ defaults 字典批量 setdefault（含本轮新增 wandb_group 默认）
147	  ├─ 预算判定：num_epoch 与 num_rollout 互斥；否则默认 num_rollout=100
148	  ├─ 保存策略：save_checkpoints=true 时按预算二选一（save_interval 或 save_final_checkpoint）
149	  ├─ 评估/追踪收尾（eval 数据、wandb_mode、路径解析）
150	  └─ RunConfig(CoreConfig(**core), miles, inference_profile=profile) → result.validate()
151	```

249	### 4.3 校验与约束：validation、constraints 与错误三分类
250	
251	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
252	
253	校验分两层：`validation.py` 提供**无状态的单值检查**（布尔、整数、时长、取值枚举、未知字段），`constraints.py` 定义**共享的约束知识**（错误分类、封闭字段表、被弃用选项的迁移指引），而涉及多字段组合的规则留在 `CoreConfig.__post_init__` 与 `RunConfig.validate` 里。所有检查都是 CPU-only：目标是让你在预约 GPU 之前就发现配置错误。
254	
255	错误三分类（[docs/miles/configuration-intro.md:40-48](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/docs/miles/configuration-intro.md#L40-L48)）：
256	
257	| 类别 | 含义 | 例子 |
258	| --- | --- | --- |
259	| Invalid configuration | 自相矛盾的设置或用错接口 | priority 字段没配 provider |
260	| Not implemented | 适配器尚未支持的功能 | `lora_rank > 0` |
261	| Not validated | 未经验证的运行时组合 | `offload_train=true` |
262	
263	三类都会在训练前拦下，**不是可以忽略的警告**。
264	
265	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
266	
267	```text
268	一个值的完整旅程（以 core.prompt_provider="priority" 为例）
269	  ├─ TOML [core] 节 → CORE_FIELDS 白名单（dataclasses.fields(CoreConfig) 的名字集）
270	  ├─ CoreConfig(**core) 构造 → __post_init__：
271	  │     choice 校验 provider ∈ {shuffle, remind, mixture, pools, priority}
272	  │     priority 三件套的类型检查（文本、非空权重表、正权重）
273	  ├─ RunConfig.validate()：

328	### 4.4 本轮更新专题：priority 采样、over_length 与 epoch 预算
329	
330	#### 4.4.1 概念说明
331	
332	本轮（`896a734 → bae4209`）给配置系统带来的三组变化，本质都是「把一个以前只能在运行时发现（或被静默忽略）的决定，提前到配置期用约束固定下来」：
333	
334	1. **priority 提示提供者**：数据行带有历史奖励优先级元数据（组 1–4），提供者按组序遍历数据。配置层的工作是用三件套字段 + 联合约束，把「用 priority 就必须说清字段名、必须全局数据集、不能叠排除/回放」说死。
335	2. **`data.over_length`**：准备阶段遇到超过提示预算的训练行时，`"fail"`（默认）整体失败，`"exclude"` 跳过并记录计数。配置层负责取值枚举校验与字段入表。
336	3. **epoch 预算**：`num_epoch` 成为与 `num_rollouts` 平级的预算选择，编译层负责互斥检查与「没有总 rollout 数时的最终存档默认」。
337	
338	#### 4.4.2 核心流程
339	
340	priority 提供者的组序遍历（运行时语义，配置只是入口）：
341	
342	```text
343	每个 sampler epoch：
344	  组 1（历史奖励有分歧）→ 组 2（未知/无历史）→ 组 3（全零且频繁截断）→ 组 4（其他常数奖励）
345	  ├─ 组内：data.seed 固定确定性洗牌（data.shuffle=false 则保持原序）
346	  ├─ 可选组内混源加权：按 source 权重抽下一个源；耗尽的源被跳过并重新归一化权重
347	  ├─ 空组跳过；请求可以跨组边界
348	  └─ 预算用普通 num_epoch / num_rollouts；priority 不强加一遍历即停
349	```
350	
351	epoch 预算的编译期 → 运行期接力：
352	
353	```text
354	编译期（本讲）                     运行期（原生 MILES）
355	num_epoch=2 ──透传 --num-epoch──►  加载准备数据后换算
356	save_final_checkpoint=True  ──►   最后一次完成的更新落盘
357	（不设 num_rollout，不造 save_interval）
358	```
359

361

436	- 配置分两层：结构化 run 文件（`RunSpec`，研究者视角）与底层 `CoreConfig` + `RunConfig`（引擎视角），`RunSpec.compile()` 是两者之间带来源追踪（origins）与冲突检测的翻译器，全程 CPU-only。

439	- 本轮更新一：priority 提供者三件套（`prompt_priority_field` / `prompt_priority_source_field` / `prompt_priority_source_weights`）进入 `CoreConfig`，联合约束要求 provider=priority、字段必填、`rollout_global_dataset=true`、不与排除表/replay 组合。

442	
443	## 7. 下一步学习建议

445	- **u8-l3（工作流与执行）**：看 `compile()` 产出的配置如何被 `workflow.py`/`driver.py` 消费——特别是 driver 返回值携带 `num_rollout` 后完成判定的变化，以及 `save_final_checkpoint` 在最后一次更新时如何落盘。

# 配置系统：TOML → RunSpec → RunConfig

> 本讲为 update 增量版本，覆盖 `896a734 → bae4209` 引入的三处配置系统变化：priority 采样相关字段、`data.over_length` 取值校验、`num_epoch` 预算与 `save_final_checkpoint` / `wandb_group` 编译默认值。旧版讲义文件此前缺失，本讲按当前 HEAD 从零补全并直接包含增量内容。

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 读懂一份 MILES run 文件（TOML）的结构：`schema_version`、必备 section、`[data]` 选择器互斥规则。
2. 沿着 `RunSpec.load → from_dict → compile → RunConfig.validate` 这条编译链，说清每个环节各做什么、错误在哪一层被拦截。
3. 会用 `python -m open_instruct.miles` 的 `plan` / `validate` 子命令与 `--set` 覆盖，在不动 GPU 的情况下排查配置错误。
4. 掌握本轮新增的三组配置语义：
   - `core.prompt_provider = "priority"` 及其约束（priority 设置要求 provider=priority、必须提供 `prompt_priority_field`、需要 `rollout_global_dataset`）；
   - `data.over_length` 只允许 `"fail"`（默认）或 `"exclude"`；
   - `training.num_epoch` 与 `training.num_rollouts` 互斥，epoch 预算的 run 默认以 `save_final_checkpoint` 在最后一次更新落盘。

## 2. 前置知识

- **TOML**：一种「节（table）+ 键值」格式的配置文件，`[data]` 定义一个节，`[[data.tasks]]` 定义数组中的一个元素节。Python 3.11+ 内置 `tomllib` 可解析。
- **dataclass**：Python 用类声明字段、由解释器自动生成 `__init__` 等方法的机制。本讲的 `RunSpec` 与 `CoreConfig` 都是 frozen（不可变）dataclass，配置一旦构造完成就不允许再改字段。
- **两层配置**：MILES 把配置分成两层——研究者面对的**结构化 run 文件**（含 `model`/`data`/`launch` 等节，描述「我要什么」），和底层运行时消费的 **Core/Miles 选项**（`[core]` 与 `[miles]`，描述「引擎怎么跑」）。前者由 `RunSpec` 承载，后者由 `CoreConfig` + `RunConfig` 承载，中间靠 `compile()` 翻译。
- **InputError**：所有用户输入错误的统一异常类型（`ValueError` 子类，见 `open_instruct/miles/errors.py`）。CLI 捕获后打印面向字段的错误信息并以退出码 2 结束。
- 建议先完成 u8-l1（MILES 总览与架构分层），了解「open-instruct 负责配置/数据/奖励集成，MILES 运行时负责 rollout 编排」的三层所有权划分。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| [open_instruct/miles/configuration/run_spec.py](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/run_spec.py) | 结构化 run 文件的加载、节级校验与编译入口；`RunSpec.compile()` 产出 `RunConfig` |
| [open_instruct/miles/configuration/config.py](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/config.py) | 底层 `CoreConfig`（Core 引擎开关）与 `RunConfig`（core+miles 合体校验、参数列表编译） |
| [open_instruct/miles/configuration/validation.py](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/validation.py) | 通用输入检查：类型、取值、未知字段的「did you mean」提示、TOML/JSON 读取、`--set` 值解析 |
| [open_instruct/miles/configuration/constraints.py](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/constraints.py) | 共享约束定义：错误三分类、各节的封闭字段表（`STRUCTURED_FIELDS`）、被弃用字段的迁移指引 |
| [open_instruct/miles/configuration/options.py](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/options.py) | 用原生 MILES 参数解析器的快照（options.json）校验/编码 miles 选项，不装 GPU 栈也能查错 |
| [open_instruct/miles/configuration/specs.py](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/specs.py) | 按文件内容选择 RunSpec 或蒸馏专用的 OPDRunSpec |
| [open_instruct/miles/__main__.py](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py) | CLI 入口：`plan/validate/train/run/status` 子命令与 `--set` 参数 |
| [configs/miles/examples/dev.toml](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/configs/miles/examples/dev.toml) | 单卡小模型冒烟示例，本轮新增 `over_length = "exclude"` |
| [docs/miles/configuration-intro.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/docs/miles/configuration-intro.md) | 维护中的配置参考：接口、优先级、默认值交互 |
| [docs/miles/data-and-evaluation.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/docs/miles/data-and-evaluation.md) | priority 组语义与 `over_length` 排除策略的运行时文档 |

---

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 RunSpec：从 TOML 到结构化运行规格

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

`RunSpec` 是研究者面对的那层配置对象：它读入 TOML run 文件，做**节级与字段级**的结构校验（哪些节存在、字段名是否认识、路径是否解析成绝对路径），但**不做**任何需要 GPU 或数据文件的工作。模块 docstring 把职责说得很清楚：校验模型/数据/训练/服务/裁判/启动设置、解析路径与覆盖，并把各节翻译成底层 MILES/Core 选项——它只「描述」准备、GPU 分配与输出位置，不执行这些阶段，因此 CLI 可以在预约算力之前先 plan 审阅一遍。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

```text
TOML 文件
  │ validation.read_document（TOML/JSON 解析）
  ▼
specs.from_dict ──training.algorithm=="opd" 且 trainer.backend=="megatron"──► OPDRunSpec（蒸馏，本讲不展开）
  │ 否则
  ▼
RunSpec.from_dict
  ├─ _apply_overrides        # --set SECTION.KEY=TOML_VALUE 逐个写入
  ├─ 顶层字段白名单 + schema_version==1 + name 字符集检查
  ├─ _table(model/output/...) # 封闭字段表（STRUCTURED_FIELDS），未知字段报错并给近似提示
  ├─ RunSpec._data           # [data]：选择器唯一性、over_length 取值、seed/shuffle、路径解析
  ├─ RunSpec._launch         # [launch]：默认值合并、Beaker 时长/优先级/挂载/保留环境变量检查
  └─ result.compile()        # 立即编译一次，加载即校验
```

关键点：**加载即编译**。`from_dict` 在构造完成后马上调用 `compile()`（[open_instruct/miles/configuration/run_spec.py:262-263](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/run_spec.py#L262-L263)），所以 `RunSpec.load()` 返回时，配置已经通过了一轮完整编译校验。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

**入口与 schema 检查**。[open_instruct/miles/configuration/run_spec.py:156-193](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/run_spec.py#L156-L193)：`load` 解析路径后调 `from_dict`；后者先深拷贝、应用覆盖，再用白名单检查顶层节名，并强制 `schema_version` 必须是整数 1，`name` 只能含字母、数字、点、下划线和连字符。这两条是最先被检查的「文件身份」。

**`--set` 覆盖的解析**。[open_instruct/miles/configuration/run_spec.py:117-135](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/run_spec.py#L117-L135)：每个覆盖按 `SECTION.KEY=TOML_VALUE` 拆分；键的分段要求小写开头（`[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`），唯一例外是三段式的 `launch.env.NAME` / `launch.secrets.NAME`——环境变量名天然大写。值本身用 `tomllib` 按 TOML 语法解析（[open_instruct/miles/configuration/validation.py:124-131](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/validation.py#L124-L131)），所以字符串要引号、布尔写裸的 `true/false`。对同一键的重复赋值，后写的覆盖先写的（普通字典赋值语义）。

**`[data]` 节：选择器互斥 + 本轮新增的 over_length 校验**。[open_instruct/miles/configuration/run_spec.py:311-325](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/run_spec.py#L311-L325)：

```python
selectors = [key for key in ("tasks", "sources", "recipe", "rl_manifest", "prompt_data") if key in data]
if len(selectors) != 1:
    raise InputError(
        f"data must select exactly one of tasks, sources, recipe, rl_manifest or prompt_data; found {selectors or 'none'}. ..."
    )
validation.choice(data.get("over_length", "fail"), "data.over_length", ("fail", "exclude"))
```

- `[data]` 必须且只能从五种数据选择器中挑一种；
- `over_length` 缺省为 `"fail"`，只接受 `"fail"` 或 `"exclude"`，写错值会得到形如 `data.over_length must be one of 'fail', 'exclude'; got 'exclud'.` 的报错。

`over_length` 之所以能出现在 `[data]`，是因为它被加入了封闭字段表：[open_instruct/miles/configuration/constraints.py:294-308](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/constraints.py#L294-L308) 中 `STRUCTURED_FIELDS["data"]` 新增了 `"over_length"`。字段表是「文档 + 校验 + 覆盖率检查」共用的单一事实源——不在表里的字段会在加载时直接报「Unknown [data] fields」。

**`[launch]` 节的默认值合并**。[open_instruct/miles/configuration/run_spec.py:369-392](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/run_spec.py#L369-L392)：workspace/budget/cluster/priority/min_runtime/timeout 等有一整套内部默认值，用 `defaults | launch` 合并（TOML 里写了就用你的）；随后校验 Beaker 风格时长（`"45m"`、`"2h30m"`，见 [open_instruct/miles/configuration/validation.py:64-84](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/validation.py#L64-L84)）、保留环境变量冲突（`RAY_ADDRESS`、`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` 等由启动器拥有）以及 weka 挂载路径不重叠。

**未知字段的「did you mean」提示**。[open_instruct/miles/configuration/validation.py:99-108](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/validation.py#L99-L108)：`fields()` 用 `difflib.get_close_matches` 对每个未知字段找一个最接近的合法名。把 `model.source` 写成 `model.sorce`，报错会附带 `'sorce': did you mean 'source'?`。

**示例文件中的 over_length**。[configs/miles/examples/dev.toml:30-32](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/configs/miles/examples/dev.toml#L30-L32) 在 `[data]` 中显式设置了 `over_length = "exclude"`，注释说明语义：排除超预算的**训练**提示并按 source 记录计数，held-out 数据仍然严格失败。

#### 4.1.4 代码实践

**实践 A：最小 run 文件的加载与两类报错观察**（CPU 即可，无需 GPU 与数据）。

1. 实践目标：亲手触发「文件身份错误」与「未知字段 did-you-mean」两类报错，熟悉错误信息风格。
2. 操作步骤：
   - 复制 `configs/miles/examples/dev.toml` 为 `my-run.toml`，把 `model.source` 改成本地任意占位路径（如 `/tmp/models/tiny-policy-hf`），`output.root` 改成 `/tmp/runs/dev`；
   - 运行 `uv run python -m open_instruct.miles validate my-run.toml`，确认能通过（结构化 validate 是 CPU-safe 的）；
   - 把 `source` 改成 `sorce` 再运行一次，记录报错；
   - 恢复后再加一行 `--set schema_version=2` 覆盖，运行 `uv run python -m open_instruct.miles validate my-run.toml --set schema_version=2`，记录报错。
3. 需要观察的现象：第二次输出应包含 `Unknown [model] fields` 与 `did you mean 'source'?`；第三次应报 `schema_version must be 1`。
4. 预期结果：错误信息都以 `my-run.toml: ...` 前缀打印（CLI 的 `parser.error` 包装），退出码为 2。
5. 若无法本地运行（如未装依赖），标「待本地验证」，改为直接阅读 [open_instruct/miles/configuration/validation.py:99-108](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/validation.py#L99-L108) 推断输出。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 `RunSpec.from_dict` 在返回前就要调用 `compile()`，而不是等用户显式调用？

**答案**：加载即校验。`RunSpec` 的职责就是保证「读进来的文件是可编译的」；若允许构造出一个未编译的非法对象，错误会推迟到 `plan`/`train` 才爆出来，排查成本更高。`compile()` 本身也承诺不加载权重和 GPU 库（见其 docstring），所以提前调用没有额外代价。

**练习 2**：`[data]` 同时写了 `tasks` 和 `prompt_data` 会发生什么？

**答案**：`_data` 中的选择器检查发现 `len(selectors) != 1`，抛出 `data must select exactly one of tasks, sources, recipe, rl_manifest or prompt_data; found ['tasks', 'prompt_data'].`，并提示移除竞争选择器或改用 `data.tasks`。

**练习 3**：`--set` 的值为什么字符串要加引号、布尔不用？

**答案**：`override_value` 把 `KEY=VALUE` 的右半部分拼成 `value=<raw>` 再用 `tomllib` 解析（[open_instruct/miles/configuration/validation.py:124-131](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/validation.py#L124-L131)）。TOML 语法里字符串必须带引号，而 `true`/`false` 本身就是合法的裸 TOML 布尔值。

---

### 4.2 编译链：RunSpec.compile 与 CoreConfig/RunConfig

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

`compile()` 是两层配置之间的翻译器：把结构化 run 文件里「研究者语言」的节（`[training]`、`[trainer]`、`[inference]`……）翻译成底层引擎消费的 `core.*` 与 `miles.*` 选项，套上工作流默认值，做跨字段的容量算术（GPU 整除、上下文长度、批大小），最后组装成 `RunConfig(CoreConfig(...), miles_options)` 并整体校验。`CoreConfig` 是 Core 训练引擎的开关集合（frozen dataclass），`RunConfig` 把它与 miles 选项字典合在一起做联合合法性检查，并能编译出真正的命令行参数列表。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

```text
RunSpec.compile(prepared=None)
  ├─ put(target, value, origin)：一切设置的唯一入口
  │    ├─ miles 键经 options.resolve_option 归一化（别名→规范名）
  │    ├─ 路径键解析为绝对路径
  │    ├─ 逐值即时校验（miles 走选项快照 + runtime_values；core 试构造 CoreConfig）
  │    └─ origins 记录来源；同目标不同值 → 冲突报错
  ├─ RUN_SECTIONS 各键分发：SPECIAL_CONTROLS / FIELD_MAP / core.* / miles.*
  ├─ [core] 与 [miles] 显式选项、compiler_cache、records、selection 依次 put
  ├─ 拓扑算术：world、rollout GPU 数、TP 整除、colocate 一致性、上下文/响应长度
  ├─ defaults 字典批量 setdefault（含本轮新增 wandb_group 默认）
  ├─ 预算判定：num_epoch 与 num_rollout 互斥；否则默认 num_rollout=100
  ├─ 保存策略：save_checkpoints=true 时按预算二选一（save_interval 或 save_final_checkpoint）
  ├─ 评估/追踪收尾（eval 数据、wandb_mode、路径解析）
  └─ RunConfig(CoreConfig(**core), miles, inference_profile=profile) → result.validate()
```

#### 4.2.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 epoch 预算不在编译期把 `num_epoch` 换算成 `num_rollout`？

**答案**：换算公式是 \[ \text{num\_rollout} = \text{num\_epoch} \times \left\lfloor \frac{\text{dataset\_size}}{\text{rollout\_batch\_size}} \right\rfloor \] 其中 `dataset_size` 要等准备好的数据加载之后才知道。编译承诺不读数据文件，所以只能把 `num_epoch` 原样透传，由原生 MILES 在数据加载后换算；保存节奏也因此退化为 `save_final_checkpoint`（只保最终更新）而不是编造 `save_interval`。

**练习 2**：`training.num_rollouts` 和 `training.num_epoch` 在 FIELD_MAP 中的待遇有何不同？

**答案**：`num_rollouts` 在 FIELD_MAP 里被重映射为 `miles.num_rollout`（[run_spec.py:51](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/run_spec.py#L51)）；`num_epoch` 不在 FIELD_MAP 里，走普通路径直接变成 `miles.num_epoch`，名字不变。

**练习 3**：`launch_warnings` 里周期性 checkpoint 的判定本轮为什么改写？

**答案**：旧代码 `miles.get("save_interval", miles["num_rollout"]) < miles["num_rollout"]` 假设 `num_rollout` 一定存在；epoch 预算下它是 None，旧式比较会出错。新代码（[run_spec.py:907-909](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/run_spec.py#L907-L909)）改为 `periodic = interval is not None and (total is None or interval < total)`，没有总 rollout 数时只要有 `save_interval` 就算周期性保存。

### 4.3 校验与约束：validation、constraints 与错误三分类

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

校验分两层：`validation.py` 提供**无状态的单值检查**（布尔、整数、时长、取值枚举、未知字段），`constraints.py` 定义**共享的约束知识**（错误分类、封闭字段表、被弃用选项的迁移指引），而涉及多字段组合的规则留在 `CoreConfig.__post_init__` 与 `RunConfig.validate` 里。所有检查都是 CPU-only：目标是让你在预约 GPU 之前就发现配置错误。

错误三分类（[docs/miles/configuration-intro.md:40-48](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/docs/miles/configuration-intro.md#L40-L48)）：

| 类别 | 含义 | 例子 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Invalid configuration | 自相矛盾的设置或用错接口 | priority 字段没配 provider |
| Not implemented | 适配器尚未支持的功能 | `lora_rank > 0` |
| Not validated | 未经验证的运行时组合 | `offload_train=true` |

三类都会在训练前拦下，**不是可以忽略的警告**。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

```text
一个值的完整旅程（以 core.prompt_provider="priority" 为例）
  ├─ TOML [core] 节 → CORE_FIELDS 白名单（dataclasses.fields(CoreConfig) 的名字集）
  ├─ CoreConfig(**core) 构造 → __post_init__：
  │     choice 校验 provider ∈ {shuffle, remind, mixture, pools, priority}
  │     priority 三件套的类型检查（文本、非空权重表、正权重）
  ├─ RunConfig.validate()：
  │     resolved_miles() 归一化 miles 选项
  │     跨字段约束（provider 与 priority 字段、rollout_global_dataset、selection/replay 互斥…）
  └─ CLI 打印 "Invalid configuration: …" 并退出码 2
```

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

**错误工厂**。[open_instruct/miles/configuration/constraints.py:16-41](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/constraints.py#L16-L41)：`constraints.error(message, category)` 生成带类别前缀的 `InputError`；`NOT_IMPLEMENTED` 会追加「欢迎带测试的实现贡献」，`NOT_VALIDATED` 会追加「欢迎用聚焦 run 帮助验证」。约束文本放在这里而不是散落在校验器里，是为了让生成式文档（`scripts/miles/generate_docs.py`）不必解析 Python 代码就能引用同一份定义。

**CoreConfig.__post_init__ 中的 priority 字段校验**。[open_instruct/miles/configuration/config.py:148-164](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/config.py#L148-L164)：`prompt_provider` 的合法取值本轮从四个扩到五个，加入 `"priority"`；三件套逐一检查——`prompt_priority_field` / `prompt_priority_source_field` 必须是非空文本，`prompt_priority_source_weights` 必须是非空的「源名 → 权重」表，每个权重要严格为正，权重总和也要严格为正（拒绝全零表）。

**RunConfig.validate 中的 priority 联合约束**。[open_instruct/miles/configuration/config.py:520-536](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/config.py#L520-L536)，这是本轮新增的整块逻辑：

- 反向约束：provider 不是 `priority` 时，任何 priority 字段被设置都报 `Priority settings require core.prompt_provider=priority`（防止字段拼错被静默忽略）；
- 正向约束（provider 为 `priority` 时）：
  1. `source_field` 与 `source_weights` 必须成对出现（要么都设要么都不设）；
  2. `prompt_priority_field` 必须提供；
  3. `rollout_global_dataset` 必须为 true（priority 提供者要全局数据集序）；
  4. 不能与冻结排除表（`[selection]`）或 prompt replay 组合。

**`num_epoch` 的正整数检查**。[open_instruct/miles/configuration/config.py:635-637](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/config.py#L635-L637)：`num_epoch` 被加入「必须为正整数」的选项列表（与 `num_rollout`、`rollout_batch_size` 等同列），传 `0`、负数或布尔值都会被拒——注意 Python 里 `True` 是 `int` 子类，所以这里用 `type(options[name]) is not int` 严格排除了布尔。

**miles 选项快照校验**。[open_instruct/miles/configuration/options.py:95-122](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/options.py#L95-L122)：`resolve_option` 用 options.json（原生解析器的快照）确认选项名存在并归一化别名；未知选项报 `Unknown MILES option: xxx; did you mean yyy?`。这让 `[training]` 节里的拼写错误（如 `num_epochx`）也能在 CPU 上立刻被抓到。

**CLI 的 validate 分支**。[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:96-104](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L96-L104)：结构化文件的 `validate` 实际执行 `config.plan()`——也就是说 validate 检查的范围等于 plan 减去 JSON 输出，连物理 GPU 分配（topology.plan）一起验了；低层 `[core]`/`[miles]` 文件的 validate 则调用原生解析器（`workflow.parse_runtime`）。两种情况都会打印一行确认语，输入和运行时检查留到 `train` 阶段。

**练习 1**：为什么 priority 的联合约束放在 `RunConfig.validate` 而不是 `CoreConfig.__post_init__`？

### 4.4 本轮更新专题：priority 采样、over_length 与 epoch 预算

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

本轮（`896a734 → bae4209`）给配置系统带来的三组变化，本质都是「把一个以前只能在运行时发现（或被静默忽略）的决定，提前到配置期用约束固定下来」：

1. **priority 提示提供者**：数据行带有历史奖励优先级元数据（组 1–4），提供者按组序遍历数据。配置层的工作是用三件套字段 + 联合约束，把「用 priority 就必须说清字段名、必须全局数据集、不能叠排除/回放」说死。
2. **`data.over_length`**：准备阶段遇到超过提示预算的训练行时，`"fail"`（默认）整体失败，`"exclude"` 跳过并记录计数。配置层负责取值枚举校验与字段入表。
3. **epoch 预算**：`num_epoch` 成为与 `num_rollouts` 平级的预算选择，编译层负责互斥检查与「没有总 rollout 数时的最终存档默认」。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

priority 提供者的组序遍历（运行时语义，配置只是入口）：

```text
每个 sampler epoch：
  组 1（历史奖励有分歧）→ 组 2（未知/无历史）→ 组 3（全零且频繁截断）→ 组 4（其他常数奖励）
  ├─ 组内：data.seed 固定确定性洗牌（data.shuffle=false 则保持原序）
  ├─ 可选组内混源加权：按 source 权重抽下一个源；耗尽的源被跳过并重新归一化权重
  ├─ 空组跳过；请求可以跨组边界
  └─ 预算用普通 num_epoch / num_rollouts；priority 不强加一遍历即停
```

epoch 预算的编译期 → 运行期接力：

```text
编译期（本讲）                     运行期（原生 MILES）
num_epoch=2 ──透传 --num-epoch──►  加载准备数据后换算
```

#### 4.4.3 源码精读

**priority 的推荐配置写法**。[docs/miles/data-and-evaluation.md:239-243](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/docs/miles/data-and-evaluation.md#L239-L243)（最小形式）与 [docs/miles/data-and-evaluation.md:265-271](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/docs/miles/data-and-evaluation.md#L265-L271)（带组内混源加权）：

```toml
[core]
prompt_provider = "priority"
prompt_priority_field = "reward_priority_olmo35_sft_hero"
# 可选：组内按源加权
prompt_priority_source_field = "workbench.source.candidate_id"
prompt_priority_source_weights = { C036 = 1.0, C046 = 2.0 }
```

**epoch 预算的文档契约**。[docs/miles/data-and-evaluation.md:294-311](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/docs/miles/data-and-evaluation.md#L294-L311)：`[training] num_epoch = 2` 或 `num_rollouts` 二选一；两者都设会被结构化 run 拒绝（正是 [run_spec.py:735-739](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/run_spec.py#L735-L739) 的报错）；都不设沿用 100 rollouts 默认。换算与「epoch 预算默认保存最终更新、显式 `save_interval` 仍可启用周期保存」的约定也写在这里。

- 排除只作用于**训练**源；held-out（评测）提示超长仍然失败；
- 保留提示文本、顺序、身份与配置的 source 比例/pool 权重；命名任务的 `train_count` 只选初始候选行，排除后不回填；
- 其余校验（token-ID/模板兼容、verifier 约束、训练/held-out 重叠检查）对包括被排除行在内的所有候选行照常执行；
- `prepared/data/manifest.json` 的 `prompt_length` 记录生效策略、整数提示上限、training 作用域，以及按 source 的 `original/excluded/retained` 计数（池计数在有池配置时一并记录）。

**测试如何钉住这些行为**：

- [open_instruct/test_miles_epoch_budget.py:14-44](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/test_miles_epoch_budget.py#L14-L44)：断言 epoch 版编译产物含 `--num-epoch` 不含 `--num-rollout`/`--save-interval`、`core.save_final_checkpoint` 为真、`training` 与 `miles` 两个位置设双预算都报 `Choose num_epoch or num_rollouts`、`save_checkpoints=false` 时不设最终存档、`num_epoch` 传 `0/-1/True` 被拒。
- [open_instruct/test_miles_priority_provider.py:125-146](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/test_miles_priority_provider.py#L125-L146)：断言 priority 配置可编译、缺 `prompt_priority_field` 报 requires、只设 priority 字段不设 provider 报 require、缺 `rollout_global_dataset` 与叠加 selection/replay 分别报错。

#### 4.4.4 代码实践

**实践 D：三个「故意写错」实验**（本讲综合实践的子任务，可独立做）。

1. 实践目标：亲眼看到三组新约束的报错文本，建立肌肉记忆。
2. 操作步骤（在实践 A 的 `my-run.toml` 上依次做，每次先恢复）：
   - 实验 1：`--set core.prompt_provider="priority"`（不提供 `prompt_priority_field`），记录报错；再补上 `--set core.prompt_priority_field="reward_priority_demo"` 看是否通过（注意还需满足单一数据输入与 `rollout_global_dataset`，dev.toml 的 `[data]` 用 `tasks` 是允许的，因为 provider 由你显式设置而 `data.sources` 未用，不会触发 put 冲突）；
   - 实验 2：`--set data.over_length="exclud"`，记录报错；
   - 实验 3：`--set training.num_epoch=2 --set training.num_rollouts=4`，记录报错。
3. 需要观察的现象：
   - 实验 1 应报 `Invalid configuration: Priority sampling requires core.prompt_priority_field`；
   - 实验 2 应报 `data.over_length must be one of 'fail', 'exclude'; got 'exclud'.`；
   - 实验 3 应报 `Choose num_epoch or num_rollouts; MILES would otherwise ignore num_epoch`。
4. 预期结果：三条都与源码/测试断言一致。实验 1 补字段后若因其他联合约束失败（例如与 `[selection]` 冲突），对照 [config.py:520-536](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/config.py#L520-L536) 逐条排查。
5. 无法运行时标「待本地验证」，以 [test_miles_priority_provider.py:125-146](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/test_miles_priority_provider.py#L125-L146) 等测试断言作为行为依据。

#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：priority 组内混源加权中，一个源的行被抽完了会发生什么？

**答案**：该源被跳过，剩余源的权重重新归一化（[docs/miles/data-and-evaluation.md:277-278](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/docs/miles/data-and-evaluation.md#L277-L278)）。权重只影响抽取顺序与早期预算曝光，不影响一个完整 sampler epoch 内每行恰好出现一次。

**练习 2**：`over_length="exclude"` 会不会让某个 `data.sources` 配置源被「掏空」？

**答案**：会失败。每个配置的 `data.sources` 条目（及每个已填充的 pool）至少要保留一行以维持采样分配，否则准备阶段在发布数据前失败（[docs/miles/data-and-evaluation.md:556-558](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/docs/miles/data-and-evaluation.md#L556-L558)）。

**练习 3**：为什么「priority 设置要求 provider=priority」的反向约束也要存在？

**答案**：防止拼写错误被静默忽略。如果只在 provider=priority 时检查三件套，那么 `[core]` 里误写的 `prompt_priority_feild`（拼错）配上默认 `shuffle` provider 会无声失效；反向约束（[config.py:520-525](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/miles/configuration/config.py#L520-L525)）让任何 priority 字段脱离 priority provider 都立即报错。（拼错字段名本身还会先被 `CORE_FIELDS` 白名单拦下。）

---

把本讲所有环节串成一次完整的「配置驱动」流程（全程 CPU，不需要 GPU 与真实数据）：

1. **准备**：复制 `configs/miles/examples/dev.toml` 为 `open-instruct-tutorial/` 之外的临时目录中的 `my-run.toml`（注意其中 [dev.toml:30-32](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/configs/miles/examples/dev.toml#L30-L32) 已有 `over_length = "exclude"`）；把 `model.source`、`output.root` 换成本地占位路径，`launch.workspace/budget` 换成你有权限的值。
2. **validate**：`uv run python -m open_instruct.miles validate my-run.toml`，应打印 `Run schema, topology and MILES/Core options validated; inputs and runtime checked during train`。
3. **plan**：`uv run python -m open_instruct.miles plan my-run.toml > plan.json`，检查输出中的 `runtime.argv`（找到 `--num-rollout 4` 与 `--save-interval 2`，对应 dev.toml 的 `num_rollouts=4`、`save_interval=2`）、`launch_warnings`、`stages` 与 `allocation`。
4. **错字段实验**：把 `[trainer] gpus = 1` 改成 `gpu = 1` 运行 validate，记录报错（会走 `Unknown MILES option` 路径并带 did-you-mean 提示）；再把 `model.source` 改成 `model.sorce` 记录另一类报错。
5. **三组约束实验**：按 4.4.4 的三个实验各做一次，记录报错原文。
6. **预算实验**：`--set training.num_epoch=2` 运行 plan，在 `plan.json` 的 `runtime.argv` 中确认出现 `--num-epoch 2`、没有 `--num-rollout` 和 `--save-interval`，并在 `runtime.core` 中确认 `save_final_checkpoint: true`。
7. **交付物**：一份表格，左列是每次故意制造的错误，右列是对应报错原文与「哪一层拦下的」（`_data` / `fields()` / `CoreConfig.__post_init__` / `RunConfig.validate` / `compile` 的互斥与冲突检查）。

## 6. 本讲小结

- 配置分两层：结构化 run 文件（`RunSpec`，研究者视角）与底层 `CoreConfig` + `RunConfig`（引擎视角），`RunSpec.compile()` 是两者之间带来源追踪（origins）与冲突检测的翻译器，全程 CPU-only。
- 加载即编译：`RunSpec.from_dict` 返回前就跑了一遍 `compile()`，绝大多数配置错误在 `plan`/`validate` 阶段就能暴露；未知字段有 did-you-mean 提示，miles 选项有解析器快照校验。
- 错误三分类（Invalid configuration / Not implemented / Not validated）由 `constraints.py` 统一定义，全部在训练前拦截，不是警告。
- 本轮更新一：priority 提供者三件套（`prompt_priority_field` / `prompt_priority_source_field` / `prompt_priority_source_weights`）进入 `CoreConfig`，联合约束要求 provider=priority、字段必填、`rollout_global_dataset=true`、不与排除表/replay 组合。
- 本轮更新二：`data.over_length` 只取 `"fail"`（默认）或 `"exclude"`；排除仅限训练侧，held-out 仍严格失败，manifest 记录 per-source 的 original/excluded/retained 计数。
- 本轮更新三：`num_epoch` 与 `num_rollouts` 互斥（`Choose num_epoch or num_rollouts`），epoch 预算透传原生换算，默认以 `core.save_final_checkpoint=true` 保存最终更新；`wandb_group` 缺省跟随 `wandb_run_name` 或 run 名。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

- **u8-l3（工作流与执行）**：看 `compile()` 产出的配置如何被 `workflow.py`/`driver.py` 消费——特别是 driver 返回值携带 `num_rollout` 后完成判定的变化，以及 `save_final_checkpoint` 在最后一次更新时如何落盘。
- **u8-l4（数据源与超长排除）**：深入 `run_data.prepare_data`，动手跑 [open_instruct/test_miles_over_length.py](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/open_instruct/test_miles_over_length.py)，观察 manifest.json 的 `prompt_length` 计数与「配置源被掏空即失败」的边界。
- **u8-l11（priority 采样专题）**：精读 `open_instruct/miles/rollout/priority_provider.py` 与 `provider_source.py`，理解组序遍历、确定性洗牌与 resume 身份校验的实现。
- 想系统了解每个选项的默认值与交互，通读 [docs/miles/configuration-intro.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/bae4209fdc541914540670c200628f67a39371ea/docs/miles/configuration-intro.md)，并用 `plan` 对照自己的 run 文件逐项核对。

Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

    ))
